$comment: Single source of truth for places, periods, data layers, natural sound, regional music and EIC visuals. Used by the app (src/data/regions.ts) and by scripts/fetch-nasa-data.mjs. Add a place here, then run `npm run fetch-data`. Facts must cite a source. Regional music is only switched on (music: "sega") where the team has researched it; otherwise musicStatus explains why there is none.

regions.name: Indian Ocean off Mauritius
regions.kidIntro: Warm blue water all around a small island in the Indian Ocean.
regions.context: Open ocean just west of Mauritius, an island about 2,000 km off the south-east coast of Africa.
regions.fact: Mauritius lies in the south-west Indian Ocean, east of Madagascar.

regions.name: Pacific Ocean off Oʻahu, Hawaiʻi
regions.kidIntro: Big Pacific waves roll in towards the islands of Hawaiʻi.
regions.context: Ocean just south of the island of Oʻahu, in the middle of the North Pacific.
regions.fact: Papahānaumokuākea, north-west of the main Hawaiian Islands, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2010 for both its nature and its Native Hawaiian cultural importance.
regions.musicNote: Hawaiian music is living Native Hawaiian heritage. EARTHSONA does not add a Hawaiian sound yet: that needs proper research and collaboration with Hawaiian musicians. Here you hear nature and data only.

regions.name: Open Central Pacific Ocean
regions.kidIntro: Deep open ocean, far from any land. Only wind and waves.
regions.context: Open water roughly 1,300 km south-east of Hawaiʻi, far from any coast.
regions.fact: The Pacific is the largest and deepest of Earth's ocean basins.
regions.musicNote: No regional music: open ocean belongs to no one culture, so you hear nature and data only.

regions.name: Black River Gorges, Mauritius
regions.kidIntro: Green hills and native forest on the island of Mauritius.
regions.context: Upland forest in south-west Mauritius, protected as the island's largest national park.
regions.fact: Black River Gorges National Park was established in 1994 and protects much of the island's remaining native forest.

factSource.label: National Parks and Conservation Service, Mauritius

regions.name: Amazon Rainforest, Brazil
regions.kidIntro: The world's biggest rainforest: thick, wet and full of life.
regions.context: Lowland rainforest in Brazil's Amazonas state, in the basin of the world's largest river by discharge.
regions.fact: The Central Amazon Conservation Complex in Amazonas state is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 2000, extended 2003).
regions.musicNote: The Amazon is home to many Indigenous peoples with their own music. EARTHSONA does not add a regional sound yet: that must be developed with Indigenous and Brazilian musicians and properly credited. Here you hear nature and data only.

regions.name: Boreal forest, Wood Buffalo, Canada
regions.kidIntro: A huge, cold northern forest of spruce and pine, snowy in winter.
regions.context: Remote boreal forest and wetland in northern Alberta, inside Canada's largest national park.
regions.fact: Wood Buffalo National Park, Canada's largest national park, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
regions.musicNote: No regional music: this experience is about the forest itself, so you hear nature and data only.

regions.name: Port Louis, Mauritius
regions.kidIntro: A warm island city where tropical rain showers come and go.
regions.context: Capital and main port of Mauritius, on the island's north-west coast in the south-west Indian Ocean.
regions.fact: Aapravasi Ghat in Port Louis, the immigration depot where indentured labourers arrived from 1849, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed 2006).

regions.name: Kyoto, Japan
regions.kidIntro: A city with four clear seasons: hot rainy summers and cold winters.
regions.context: Former imperial capital in a basin surrounded by hills on the island of Honshu.
regions.fact: The Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto (Kyoto, Uji and Otsu Cities) were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1994.
regions.musicNote: Japan has many regional music traditions. EARTHSONA does not add a Japanese sound yet: an original palette needs research with Japanese musicians and proper credit, not a stereotype. Here you hear nature and data only.

regions.name: Ross Island, Antarctica
regions.kidIntro: The coldest place on Earth: ice, snow and strong winds.
regions.context: Ross Island at the edge of the Ross Ice Shelf, home to research stations.
regions.fact: The Antarctic Treaty, signed in 1959, sets Antarctica aside for peaceful purposes and scientific research.
regions.musicNote: No regional music: Antarctica has no native population, so you hear nature and data only.

eic.$comment: Official NASA Earth Information Center visuals (SVS ids from the EIC gallery 40467 and the EIC Daily Visualizations gallery 40512). `relation` says honestly how each visual relates to the sound.

ocean.relation: Same topic and the same NASA dataset family as the sound (MUR sea surface temperature). The EIC map shows the whole planet for recent days; the sound plays one point over 2020–2024.
Shows where the ocean is warmer or cooler than usual, the same idea as the harmony layer. It covers recent days worldwide, not the years in the sound.

forest.relation: Shows how TALL forests are, measured by laser from the International Space Station. The sound uses a different measurement, MODIS greenness (NDVI/EVI): tall and green are related but not the same.
The same measurement as the melody (NDVI greenness), shown worldwide for a recent period; the sound plays one forest over 2020–2024.

pulse.relation: Rain and clouds from NASA's GEOS weather model for recent days: a model, like the POWER values in the sound. The sound uses POWER rainfall for one place over 2015–2024.
Near-surface air temperature from the GEOS model for recent days, the same variable as the melody (air temperature at 2 m), for the whole planet.

imagery.$comment: NASA GIBS WMS snapshots bundled by `npm run fetch-data -- --only=imagery`.
